## 

#### Abstracting Social Influence

Let $x_i(t) \in \mathbb{R}$ be the opinion of agent $i$ at time $t$. 

![](../_img/kernel-inference/triad.png){height=2.5in  fig-align="center"}

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \underbrace{\color{#d0bfff}{x_1}(t+1) - \color{#a5d8ff}{x_1}(t)}_{\text{opinion change } \delta_i(t+1)} = \overbrace{\lambda}^{\text{Learning rate}} \underbrace{\frac{\color{#fa5252}{x_2}(t) + \color{#ffc9c9}{x_3}(t)}{2}}_{\text{average opinion of neighbors}}
\end{aligned}
$$



## {.split-40}


#### More generally, 

::: {.column}

<br><br><br>

![](../_img/kernel-inference/network.png){width="100%"}

[DeGroot (1974). "Reaching a consensus." *JASA*]{.footnote}

:::


::: {.column}

<br><br><br><br><br>

Let $\partial i$ be the set of neighbors of agent $i$. 

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \underbrace{x_i(t+1) - x_i(t)}_{\text{opinion change } \delta_i(t+1)} &= \lambda \underbrace{\frac{1}{|\partial i|}\sum_{j \in \partial i} x_j(t)}_{\text{average opinion of neighbors}} \\ 
\end{aligned}
$$

:::


## {.split-50}

#### A realistic model?

::: {.column}

<br><br>

![](../_img/kernel-inference/autokinetic.png)

:::

::: {.column}

<br><br><br>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig.width: 6
#| fig.height: 4

library(tidyverse)

x = c(0.5, 2, 8)
A = matrix(c(0, 1, 1,
             1, 0, 1,
             1, 1, 0), nrow=3, byrow=TRUE)
lambda = 0.5

df = tibble(t = 0, agent = 1:3, opinion = x)
for(t in 1:3){
  x = x + 0.5 * (A %*% x / rowSums(A) - x)
  df = bind_rows(df, tibble(t=t, agent=1:3, opinion=x))
}

df |> ggplot() +
  geom_line(data=df, aes(x=t, y=opinion, linetype=factor(agent)), size=1.5) +
#   scale_color_manual(values=c("#d0bfff", "#fa5252", "#ffc9c9")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position="none") +
  labs(x="Model timestep", y="Opinion") + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 10)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values=c("dotted", "dashed", "solid")) + 
  ggtitle("DeGroot (1974) model")
```

:::

<br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br> <br>

On a connected social graph where all agents listen (at least a little bit) to all their neighbors, DeGroot dynamics always converge to a consensus. 

## {background-image="../_img/kernel-inference/polarized-report.png" background-size="contain" background-position="center" background-repeat="no-repeat"}


## 

#### Generalizing with Influence Kernels

::: {.column}

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \delta_i(t+1) &= x_i(t+1) - x_i(t) \\
    &= \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|}\sum_{j \in \partial i} x_j(t)   \quad \quad (\text{DeGroot})
\end{aligned}
$$

![](../_img/shared/downarrow.png){fig-align="center" height=30}

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \delta_i(t+1) &= x_i(t+1) - x_i(t) \\
    &=  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} \color{#A4303F}{K(\underbrace{ |x_j(t) - x_i(t)| }_{\text{unsigned distance } d_{ij}})} x_j(t)
\end{aligned}
$$



:::

::: {.column}

<br> <br> <br> 

- *Attraction*: $K(d_{ij}) > 0$
- *Repulsion*: $K(d_{ij}) < 0$
- *Indifference*: $K(d_{ij}) = 0$

We recover DeGroot dynamics if $K(y) \equiv 1$.

[There are other possible ways to normalize this]{.footnote}

:::

## {.split-60}

#### Kernel Zoo: DeGroot Dynamics

::: {.column}

<br>

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \color{#A4303F}{k(d)} &= 1
\end{aligned}
$$

![](../_img/kernel-inference/fig_kernel_atlas_simplified_degroot.png){.absolute top=210 left=0 width="100%"}

:::

::: {.column}

<br>

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i 
    =  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d_{ij})} x_j 
\end{aligned}
$$



*Simulated on a random graph with a small amount of random noise incorporated into the update for interest.* 

:::


## {.split-60}

#### Kernel Zoo: Bounded Confidence

::: {.column}

<br> 

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d)} &= \mathbb{1}[d < \phi]
\end{aligned}
$$

![](../_img/kernel-inference/fig_kernel_atlas_bounded_confidence.png){.absolute top=210 left=0 width="100%"}

:::

::: {.column}

<br> 

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i 
    =  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d_{ij})} x_j 
\end{aligned}
$$



Creates sustained opinion clusters at approximately distance $\phi$.


  
[Hegselmann & Krause (2002). "Opinion dynamics and bounded confidence models, analysis, and simulation." *JASSS*.
<br><br>
Deffuant et al. (2000). "Mixing beliefs among interacting agents." *Advances in Complex Systems*.]{.footnote}




:::


## {.split-60}

#### Kernel Zoo: ✨Sigmoidal✨ Bounded Confidence

::: {.column}

<br> 

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d)} &= \left(1 + \exp \left[\phi_1(d^2 - \phi_0^2)\right]\right)^{-1}
\end{aligned}
$$

![](../_img/kernel-inference/fig_kernel_atlas_sigmoidal_bounded_confidence.png){.absolute top=210 left=0 width="100%"}

:::

::: {.column}

<br> 

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i 
    =  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d_{ij})} x_j 
\end{aligned}
$$


Converges to bounded-confidence dynamics with radius $\phi_0$ as $\phi_1 \rightarrow \infty$ and to DeGroot dynamics as $\phi_1 \rightarrow 0$.

Allows linear stability analysis of bounded-confidence type behavior. 

[Brooks, **PSC**, Porter (2024). "Emergence of polarization in a sigmoidal bounded-confidence model of opinion dynamics." *SIADS*.]{.footnote}

:::



## {.split-60}

#### Kernel Zoo: Smooth Attraction-Repulsion

::: {.column}

<br>

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d)} = \left(1 - \frac{d^2}{\phi^2}\right) \exp\left(\frac{d^2}{-2\phi}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

![](../_img/kernel-inference/fig_kernel_atlas_rzb.png){.absolute top=210 left=0 width="100%"}

:::

::: {.column}

<br> 

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i 
    =  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} \color{#A4303F}{k_\phi(d_{ij})} x_j 
\end{aligned}
$$


No standard attraction-repulsion kernel; we use a Ricker wavelet. 

Generates close-knit communities that slowly diverge.

[Ryan (1994). "Ricker, Ormsby, Klauder, Butterworth - A Choice of Wavelets." *CSEG Recorder*.]{.footnote}

:::

## {.split-30}



#### How do we learn the kernel from data?

::: {.column}

<br> <br> 

Easiest case: for each $i$ there is only one neighbor $j$. 

![](../_img/kernel-inference/pair.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i
    \approx  \lambda \color{#228be6}{k_\phi}(|\color{#fd7e14}{x_j} - \color{#fd7e14}{x_i}|) \color{#fd7e14}{x_j}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.column}

<br> <br> 

![](../_img/kernel-inference/adams_p08_scatter_only.png){fig-align="center"}

[Adams, White, and Araujo (2022). "Person-to-person opinion dynamics: An empirical study using an online game." *PLoS ONE*.]{.footnote}

:::

## {.split-30}

#### A more complex case: multiple neighbors

::: {.column}

<br> 

![](../_img/kernel-inference/mini-neighborhood.png)
$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i
    &\approx  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} \color{#228be6}{k_\phi}(|\color{#fd7e14}{x_j} - \color{#fd7e14}{x_i}|) \color{#fd7e14}{x_j}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.column}

<br> <br> 

![](../_img/kernel-inference/plos_gauging_scatter_and_conditional_mean.png)

:::

<br> <br> <br> 



[
  At each timestep <br> 
  each agent [***always***]{.alert}  interacts <br> 
  with [***all***]{.alert-2} of their neighbors.
]{style="font-size: 2em;"} 






:::

::: {.column}

<br> <br>


$$
\begin{aligned}
  \delta_i
    &=  \lambda \frac{1}{|\partial i|} \sum_{j \in \partial i} k_\phi(d_{ij}) x_j
\end{aligned}
$$

### Our Model
